News.title: Russian minister ‘secretly flees to US after dodging FSB’ in first escape of high-ranking Putin official
News.content:
ON THE RUN Russian minister ‘secretly flees to US after dodging FSB’ in first escape of high-ranking Putin official

A RUSSIAN minister has secretly fled to the US after dodging Vladimir Putin’s feared security forces, reports say – marking the first escape of a top Kremlin official.

Denis Butsaev, 49, has reportedly abandoned the Russian tyrant’s regime after being fired from his post as Deputy Minister of Natural Resources.





The minister reportedly travelled to Belarus before making the journey to America.

He was previously fired from his post on April 22 – and is said to have gone on the run on the same day, according to local media.

The exact date he left Russia is still unconfirmed, with some reports indicating he left as early as April 18, before he was officially dismissed.

Butsaev has reportedly fled amid a growing investigation into supposed top-level corruption.

The probe is understood to involve Butsaev and other high-ranking figures at the Russian Environmental Operator – a government agency he previously led.

Butsaev’s departure marks the first known case of a sitting official of such high rank fleeing Putin’s regime.

News.title: I walked into my new three-bed home to find it mould-ridden with mattress soaked in BLOOD… it’s like a crime scene
News.content:
HOUSE OF HORROR I walked into my new three-bed home to find it mould-ridden with mattress soaked in BLOOD… it’s like a crime scene

A YOUNG woman has spoken of her horror after moving into a mould-ridden home with a blood-soaked mattress.

Charlotte Preston, 22, said her new three-bedroom terraced home in Norwich, Norfolk, looked like a “crime scene”.





The student, who pays £483 along with her two housemates, was left stunned after discovering the mattress in her room was “soaked through with a massive blood stain”.

She is fighting for her estate agent to fix a list of urgent repairs and get rid of the black damp that covers her walls.

And she claims she was even told by her landlord that “clean is subjective”.

Charlotte said: “The whole place looks condemned.

“We found a mattress soaked through with a massive blood stain, and the front door needed repairs.

“I work with people who suffer from addiction so I am well-versed in the risks bloodborne diseases carry.

“It looked like a crime scene.

“The house smelt really strange too. There was grease all over the top of the oven and inside.”



Charlotte said she had no choice but to pay for last-minute accommodation on her move-in date last September.

She said her estate agents, Abbotts, told her she could collect the keys at midday on September 1 but was left waiting for a further four hours.

But she says they refused to give them to her until 4.20pm forcing her removal men to wait around.

When she entered the “filthy” house, she was greeted by black mould.



Charlotte, who visited the Abbotts branch in Norwich in person, said: “I was told they didn’t have time for a cleaner to come in as the previous tenancy had ended the day before.

“They said they would arrange for a cleaner to come.

“It took seven days until I could move in. I still have the mould problem now.

“The garden was left overgrown, the toilet wouldn’t flush – I had to wait 15 minutes for it to refill and use a kettle to top up the water.”



Charlotte continued: “After I discovered the mattress, I knew I couldn’t sleep there.

“Abbotts offered to put me up in alternative accommodation but my landlord refused.

“If it wasn’t for the UEA, where I am studying, I would have been out on the streets – I wish I had never signed my contract.”



Charlotte says her university gave her three nights of accommodation for free but was forced to fork out £85 for further nights until the issue was resolved.

Abbotts has offered Charlotte and the two other tenants £150 of compensation.

But Charlotte wants £480 for her and her two housemates, which would cover the week she says they could not live there.

She added: “It seems as if Abbotts have no empathy for students like myself.

“Students deserve better in terms of how they’re treated by estate agents especially with the Renters Rights’ Act.”



A spokesman for Abbotts said: “As the managing agent, we act on behalf of the landlord and must operate accordingly.

“However, we are dedicated to support all parties involved and appreciate the tenant perspective.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We have worked hard to find an appropriate solution between all parties.

“Based on our review, we are satisfied that appropriate steps have been taken.”

News.title: Two American soldiers vanish during African Lion 2026 drills in Morocco sparking massive search operation
News.content:
DESERT HUNT Two American soldiers vanish during African Lion 2026 drills in Morocco sparking massive search operation

TWO American troops have vanished while taking part in a military exercises in Morocco, sparking desperate rescue efforts.

The soldiers were reported missing near the Cap Draa Training Area, close to the southern city of Tan Tan on May 2.





Authorities have not yet released further details about the circumstances of their disappearance.

A US official, speaking on the condition of anonymity, said the service members were involved in a hiking accident, according to Star and Stripes.

The two troops reportedly fell into the ocean during the incident.

Search efforts – including ground, air and maritime assets – are understood to be ongoing.



A statement by United States Africa Command said: “Our focus is on the service members involved and their families.

“Additional information will be provided as it becomes available.”

The two soldiers were taking part in African Lion 2026 when they disappeared.

African Lion 2026 is the US Africa Command’s largest annual joint military exercise.



It is designed to strengthen cooperation between US forces, Nato allies, and African partner nations.

Hosted across Morocco, Ghana, Senegal, and Tunisia, the exercise brings together thousands of personnel to train side by side in realistic scenarios.

The war games exercise started in April and is scheduled to end in early May.

The Pentagon has not yet released the identities of the missing soldiers.

News.title: Inside disturbing world of ‘Tinder for teens’ apps with predators free to groom, abuse & extort children as young as 11
News.content:
WITH names like Wizz, Purp, and Whipd, these innocent‑sounding apps, where children can connect with friends, might not initially ring alarm bells.

But take a closer look, and parents will discover the chilling world of “friend-making” phone apps being dubbed “Tinder for teens”. A disturbing investigation by The Sun found that it was easy for anyone, of any age, to bypass checks on some of them, making it, experts warn, a playground for paedophiles who were free to groom, blackmail and sextort victims.



Despite being advertised as friend-making platforms, many are designed exactly like adult dating apps, such as Tinder, Hinge or Bumble.

They feature eerily similar mechanics, allowing children to swipe on profiles they like, match with strangers, and privately message – even offering them the chance to pay for extra swipes if they run out.

It’s therefore hardly surprising that many youngsters often treat these sites as teen dating apps.



But while the dating-app style layout is disturbing, some of the platforms’ lax age-verification checks and the ability to connect with strangers UK-wide or even globally mean the apps have become a cesspit for predators, experts say.

In its description, Purp claims it is the “best place to make new friends from all over the world”.

Whipd, on the other hand, says users simply need to “swipe, meet, [and] chat” to find “new besties with similar vibes”.

All of these apps say they are “safe spaces” for children – and try to support their claims with online tools such as age verification.

But after The Sun carried out its own investigation into these apps, we found that age checks could still be bypassed by adults who want to gain access to child-only spaces.



To make an account, users are asked to enter their name, age, and other typical dating app-style questions like their interests, hobbies and height.

They are then asked to upload a selfie to prove their age.

But The Sun found that someone over 18 could easily bypass these age estimation systems to access child-only spaces.

Using Purp, our 24-year-old reporter was able to pose as a 14-year-old and access the app’s under-18 features.



As well as offering a typical swipe and like matching system, Purp also features a unique public community chatroom where dozens of children interact with apparent under-18 profiles, click on their profiles and match.

On Hoop – another swipe-based “friend-making app” where users match but are then instructed to chat over different social media platforms like Snapchat – we were also able to create a teenager account.

The sign-up process took just minutes and was as simple as entering a fake name, age, profile picture and age verification selfie.

Additionally, we were able to make an account on Whipd by lying during a similar process.

The Sun was not able to access Wizz – which told us it has introduced stricter age verification methods.



‘They asked for nude photos’

In the UK, children as young as 11 have reportedly been inundated with vile sexual messages on apps like Wizz.

Last year, Childline told The Sun that an 11-year-old girl reported to them: “I was using Wizz app with my friends when someone (who I thought was 13)… pm’d [private messaged] me.

“They asked me for a nude photo and threatened me, saying that they knew where I lived, so I sent it to them.”

Reports like these have raised concerns that children under the age of 13

may also be able to bypass age checks and access spaces with older strangers.



Several experts told The Sun many age checks on these apps are flimsy, and in some cases may even be deliberately weak, as stricter methods like passport or driving licence uploads can deter younger users unwilling to share sensitive documents.

More robust systems – such as ID verification combined with biometric matching – are also more expensive than AI-powered facial age estimates, giving platforms an incentive to rely on cheaper, less rigorous checks.

Executive Director of the National Centre on Sexual Exploitation (NCOSE) Haley McNamara said apps open the door wide with soft checks to attract users – but only tighten rules later when pressure mounts from regulators or media scrutiny.

She also told The Sun that the apps created “direct pathways for grooming, abuse, and sextortion”.



McNamara says: “They mimic, they get their playbook from dating apps in their setup.”

She continues: “The importance is they should just not be connecting minors with strangers on the app as a premise.

“It’s an unsafe premise. So that’s, at the end of the day, the problem.”



Teodora Pavkovic, a director at online safety organisation Linewize, tells The Sun: “While each app is a bit different, the key similarities are: matching users based on common features, the ability to select or reject user profiles, and a focus on connecting with new people.”

She adds: “Parents need to keep in mind that their children will be interacting with strangers, that age-verification is not a foolproof safety mechanism, and that even though these platforms weren’t designed to be dating apps, many young people use them for that purpose.

“The combination of these features can pose a risk to young users.”

McNamara also emphasised that, even if age checks were better, the main purpose of these apps is to “connect minors with strangers, which every parent should be very alarmed about”.

She adds: “Hoop, Whipd, these apps are inherently dangerous, especially because they’re marketed towards kids.”



Predators in Britain have been jailed for using Wizz to target innocent children.

In 2023, Shabaz Hussain, 23, was handed a nine-year prison sentence after posing as a child on Wizz and manipulating a 12-year-old girl into building a relationship with him – eventually meeting and sexually abusing her.

And just last year, Steven MacMillan, 53, was jailed for 20 months after using the app to send a 13-year-old girl “graphic and disturbing” sexual voice notes.



In 2024, Wizz was banned entirely from the App Store and Google Play after watchdogs flagged rampant sexual exploitation on the app.

The NCOSE said Wizz had “connected children with strangers, leading to grooming and abuse”.

Other similar apps were still allowed to operate – and more are still springing up constantly.

Young Wizz users were also vulnerable to “financial sextortion” scams, another study by the National Contagion Research Institute found.

It said: “Some victims report being targeted by sextortion within minutes of joining the app, suggesting that criminals have saturated Wizz.”



The report also said there had been “a high frequency of complaints that the app [Wizz] is serving pornographic ads to minors”.

Wizz was later put back on the App Store and Google Play after it claimed to have improved its age verification checks – systems that experts say are still possible to bypass.

After all, AI-based facial age estimation scans provide an estimate, but never definitive proof.

There are, therefore, mounting concerns that under-13s can access spaces with users as old as 17 if age checks fail – or that older people are able to access younger spaces, as The Sun found out.

Pavkovic says: “Currently, age checks are, unfortunately, not 100 per cent effective.



“The technology does continue to improve, though.”

McNamara warned that youngsters on these apps risk being pressured to move conversations off-platform – onto social media sites such as on Snapchat or Instagram.

They may then be tricked into sharing explicit images, leaving them vulnerable to depraved sextortion schemes where predators use those photos to blackmail them.



Tragically, some children have even taken their own lives within hours of being tricked online, McNamara said, citing one case linked to Instagram.

She told The Sun: “There are many cases of children who’ve been contacted, and within a couple of hours… some of them have even taken such drastic choices as death by suicide.

“Sextortionists are often pressuring – applying intense psychological pressure – on those children to either send more child sexual abuse materials or to send money.”

‘It’s designed like a Tinder for teens’

There are dozens of alleged sexual assault cases linked to Wizz, Purp, and other friend-making apps.

In February this year, a 28-year-old man was arrested in New York and accused of raping a 14-year-old girl he met online.



Police said he first met her on the Purp app.

In 2023, 31-year-old Ryan Austin Lauless of Colorado was jailed for 84 years after pleading guilty to multiple counts of sexual exploitation.

He used apps like Purp and Yubo to target at least 84 children across the US and in several other countries, court docs show.

A 20-year-old Florida man was arrested in 2024 after cops said he was speaking to a 14-year-old girl on Wizz while pretending to be 16.

Additionally, Alejandro Porras, 28, from Cook County in Chicago, was jailed for three years for posing as a teenager on Wizz to lure and sexually abuse underage girls in 2025.



A former US Marine was also arrested just last year in Hawaii for allegedly sexually assaulting an 11-year-old after meeting her on Wizz.

Véronique Béchu, a director at online safety organisation e-Enfance, said her organisation in France had dealt with recent reports of sextortion and revenge porn through Wizz among victims as young as 15.

After facing huge backlash late last year, Wizz has now increased its minimum age for users to 16, but it’s still impossible to guarantee the ages of its users.



Béchu, a former cop who combated child abuse for decades, told The Sun: “We know that kids can send nudes of themselves, so this can be a way for sexual predators to get with kids to obtain child sexual abuse material.

“It’s designed like a Tinder for teens.”

Brandon Guffey, whose 17-year-old son took his own life after becoming a victim of sextortion through social media, said the predators responsible for his child’s death would no doubt have used teenage “friend-making” apps to target children if they were still operating today.

The Congressman told The Sun: “A predator’s always going to go where their prey is, and if children are going to these dating apps, then they’re going to be there.”

Now helping other victims, he added: “Whenever I first started dealing with sextortion, a lot of the cases I was dealing with were through Wizz.



“That’s slowed down now in terms of Wizz because they have raised their age limit recently to 16, but the threat still exists with other companies.”

Experts also pointed to a growing problem, a revolving door of new platforms ready to take the place of those that get taken down in the face of mounting media pressure.

Yubo, formerly called Yellow, was once the most popular teenage platform – but after facing mounting concerns over its safety, it was forced to increase its minimum age to 18 last November.



Many other sites have since filled the void it left behind.

Apps like Hoop and Purp may dominate for now – but if they introduce stricter age limits, experts warn it could simply trigger a fresh wave of copycat platforms stepping in to fill the gap.

And McNamara said: “Dozens and dozens of copycat apps that are rated 12 plus, that have essentially the same structure and goals.”

Béchu added: “If we shut down an app, there are others that will blow up.”

A spokesperson from Wizz told The Sun: “Every person who creates a Wizz account goes through facial age estimation powered by Yoti, the same technology trusted by the UK Home Office and NHS, before they can interact with anyone on the platform.



“That system has a 99.95–99.98 per cent accuracy rate.

“If there’s any discrepancy between the age someone enters and their estimated age, they’re required to submit ID verification before they can proceed.”

Whipd told us the “safety of our community and particularly our younger users is our highest priority”.

A spokesperson said: “While our systems are designed to categorize users into age-appropriate groups (minors vs. adults) and apply strict safety rules accordingly, we recognize that no digital verification system is entirely immune to intentional deception by an adult.”

They claimed to “mitigate these risks” by using platform-level integration, human moderation, AI scanning, and verification checks.



The platform added: “We take your feedback seriously and are constantly evolving our technology to prevent bad actors from circumventing these safeguards.”

The Sun reached out to Hoop, Purp, and Yubo for comment.

News.title: Brit, 50, becomes first person to pull 2-tonne car with his PENIS while on fire… weeks after towing motor with testicles
News.content:
A BRIT has said he is the first person in the world to pull a two-tonne car with his penis – while on fire.

John Stephenson pulled the French police car 40 metres along a street in Halifax, West Yorkshire, on April 30.





The 50-year-old had made headlines weeks prior, after he also pulled a car using his testicles.

John said: “I’ve pulled a car with my testicles before and I’ve pulled a car on fire – so I thought why not combine the both, but this time do it with my penis.

“I won’t lie – it did hurt quite a bit.

“But my mind was focused on being on fire and I just ploughed on and pulled it for around 40 metres.



“I doused myself in lighter fuel and the wind was against me a bit, so it took a couple of attempts.

“I’ve got a few marks down there, but everything is still intact, so hopefully no harm done.

“People think I’m a bit mad – but I like to set myself challenges.

“I did my research and nobody in the world has ever done this before.

“There is a serious side to it too – I’m raising awareness of prostate cancer and bullying in schools.



“I’m also raising money for Ruddis Retreat in Huddersfield which provides holidays for families of children with cancer.”

John, from Lincolnshire, pulled the Renault Clio RS using a tow rope attached to his penis.

The martial arts expert and former bare-knuckle fighter had previously made headlines for pulling a similar stunt by towing a car using his testicles on February 27.

He has also pulled an American police car 20 metres across a West Yorkshire storage yard while his head was on fire, on March 13.

He decided to combine the two in the new record attempt, with the goal to raise awareness of men’s mental health issues.



John said he is the first person in the world to have pulled off the crazy feat.

He also holds the world record for reeling off 300 punches in 30 seconds, all while holding 1kg dumbbells in each hand.

Other records to his name through Official Record Breakers involve performing six martial arts kicking techniques in less than five and a half seconds and a number involving pulling or lifting vehicles.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Alongside his crazy and unique world records, he is also an author and has previously been inducted into a number of Martial Arts Halls of Fame.

News.title: Fruit yoghurt ads ‘could be banned in government clampdown on junk food’ as firms blast ‘counter-intuitive’ new rules
News.content:
YOG SLOG Fruit yoghurt ads ‘could be banned in government clampdown on junk food’ as firms blast ‘counter-intuitive’ new rules

FRUIT yoghurt ads reportedly may be banned under Labour’s clampdown on junk food.

Under government health plans, yoghurts with added fruit could be deemed “unhealthy” and subject to the 9pm watershed.





The red tape is part of the government’s 10-Year Health Plan for England, setting to “raise the healthiest generation of children ever”.

But food giants have slammed the proposals as “nonsensical” and “counter intuitive”, reports The Telegraph.

The UK Nutrient Profiling Model (NPM) was updated to include “free sugars” that are released from fruit and veg when mashed or pureed – meaning fruit yoghurts could be put in the same category as added sweeteners .

Public consultations are underway to assess how to apply the new model to the “junk food” advertising and in-store promotions ban.

This means product ads for fruit yoghurts could be subject to the 9pm watershed ban, which stops material unfit for children being shown in daytime hours.

Major companies such as Danone and Nestlé have raised the alarm over Labour’s heightened chokehold – warning they may be forced to rethink recipes or even axe products altogether.



Experts have warned the proposals are likely to push up food prices for shoppers.

Professor Chris Whitty, Chief Medical Officer for England, said: “Free sugars are associated with increased levels of childhood obesity and other health harms, putting children’s health at risk for the rest of their lives.

“Applying the updated NPM to advertising and promotions will reduce marketing of unhealthy products at children, helping to reduce excess free sugar consumption and benefiting current children’s health now and in the future.”

Firms are calling for the plan to be scrapped with worries consumers will shift to buying cakes and biscuits or adding honey and syrup to plain yoghurts.

A spokesman for Danone North Europe said they support steps to improve public health but warned of the risk of “unintended consequences for customers”.



Danone’s Activia Mango Yogurt and Nestlé’s The Ski Smooth Strawberry and Raspberry, all currently classed as not high in fat, salt or sugar, could be deemed “unhealthy” due to the fruit puree.

Danone and Nestlé are reported to be assessing proposals and may eventually have to look into reformulation.

Yeo Valley Organic said it supported action against unhealthy foods but warned it would be “counter-intuitive” for “naturally nutritious” products like yoghurts with fruit to be treated in the same was as UPFs.

This comes after previous warnings that fresh tomatoes could be removed from Dolmino pasta sauces as part of the same rule change.

Critics claim the impact assessment justifying the switch to the updated nutrient model is “not fit for purpose” and “lacks proper and thorough representation” of the impact the policy would have on public health, reports The Grocer.



A Department of Health and Social Care spokesperson said: “As part of the 10 Year Health Plan this government committed to supporting parents to raise the healthiest generation of children ever.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The current system is based on a nutrient profiling model more than 20 years old, which does not reflect modern dietary advice, which is why we have consulted on updating it.

“Since 2015, guidance has been clear that children should eat less free sugar and more fibre. The updated model reflects this and better balances beneficial nutrients against salt, sugar and saturated fat.”

News.title: Full list of 10 ‘fastest declining’ dog breeds in the UK from Labradors to Bulldogs – is your pup on the list?
News.content:
A NEW list has revealed the dog breeds that have seen the fastest decline in the UK.

The analysis looks at registrations between 2024 and 2025, with some popular pooches seeing surprising drop-offs.



Examining statistics from the Royal Kennel Club for the past calendar year, Briefcase found that the French Bulldog had the steepest drop-off in registrations in 2025.

There were 6,000 fewer French Bulldogs registered, a major fall from the 13,789 recorded the year before.



Behind the “fastest declining breed” was the Retriever (Labrador) with 4,222 fewer registrations.

This was followed by the Dachshund (Miniature Smooth Haired) with a drop of 2,756 and the Spaniel (Cocker) with 1,559 fewer registrations.

Rounding out the top five was the classic Bulldog, which saw a decline of 1,154 over the year period.

Meanwhile, miniature Schnauzers, Spaniels (English Springer), German Shepherds, Border Terriers, and Pugs completed the top 10 list.



It comes ahead of new breeding regulations in the UK, created to ensure the health of breeds such as the French Bulldog as with new standards are introduced on features such as flat faces, skin wrinkles, and short legs.

On the other side of things, Dachshunds (Miniature Long Haired) led the rise in registrations with an increase of 244, this was followed by Jack Russell Terriers with 185 and Italian Greyhounds with 118.

A Briefcase spokesman said: “Looking at year-over-year movement reveals a very different story from a straight popularity ranking, with several of the UK’s most established favourites seeing steep declines while some smaller breeds continue to gain momentum.

“The figures suggest dog-breed preferences are shifting meaningfully, even if the biggest breeds still dominate overall registration totals.”

News.title: Iran gives Trump 4-week deadline to end Strait of Hormuz blockade as president warns of strikes if regime ‘misbehaves’
News.content:
IRAN has given Donald Trump a four-week deadline to end the Strait of Hormuz blockade – as the US president warns of fresh strikes if the regime “misbehaves”.

The latest 14-point plan from Tehran will put nuclear negotiations on hold until the two sides agree on other issues including the key waterway and Western sanctions.





It comes as the Strait of Hormuz saga continues to strain global energy markets – sending oil reserves towards a “tipping point“, analysts say.

The new proposal includes terms such as: both sides lifting blockades in the trade strait, an end to the war in Lebanon, the release of frozen Iranian assets, and US compensation as well as the lifting of sanctions.

Tehran has given Trump a one-month deadline to respond to the latest plan, Axios reported.

Negotiations on Iran‘s nuclear ambitions would then be discussed at a later date, the plans outline.



The US president has appeared to reject the plan in another Truth Social post.

He fumed: “I will soon be reviewing the plan that Iran has just sent to us, but can’t imagine that it would be acceptable in that they have not yet paid a big enough price for what they have done to Humanity, and the World, over the last 47 years.”



Trump said he was also waiting to hear the exact wording of Iran’s new proposal.

He is also keeping the option of launching fresh strikes or a ground invasion in Iran on the table.

Addressing the potential resumption of attacks on Iranian soil, Trump said: “I don’t want to say that. I mean, I can’t tell that to a reporter.



“If they misbehave, if they do something bad, right now we’ll see. But it’s a possibility that could happen.”

Top Iranian officials have warned that war is likely to restart.

One top chief said: “Renewed conflict between Iran and the United States is likely.”

The comments came after Trump suggested the US might be “better off” without a deal at all.

On Sunday, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said the US faced a choice between an “impossible” military operation or a “bad deal” with the Islamic republic.



The regime said: “Trump must choose between an impossible operation or a bad deal with the Islamic Republic of Iran.”

It cited what it described as a “shift in tone” from China, Russia, and Europe towards Washington as well as what it called an Iranian “deadline” over the US naval blockade.

Experts are also warning that the world will reach a “tipping point” in global crude oil reserves by the end of May – which could send prices soaring in summer.

Negotiations – now almost a month after the ceasefire was first unveiled – remain in limbo.

Nuclear energy and a “management plan” for the Strait of Hormuz appear to be the most contentious points for both parties.



This comes after Trump said on Friday that – “on a human basis” – he did not prefer the military course of action and told congressional leaders he did not need their permission to extend the war beyond a deadline set by law for that day because the ceasefire had “terminated” hostilities.

Trump is not the only one sceptical about the negotiations.

Senior Iranian military and security officials have also expressed pessimism about the prospects for compromise.

Deputy Brigadier General Mohammad Jafar Asadi and an Iranian security official both described renewed military conflict between Iran, the US and Israel as “likely” and emphasised that Iranian armed forces remain on full alert.

Analysts from the Institute for the Study of War warned that the regime has in fact not altered its position on key matters at all.



As in previous proposals, Iran proposes postponing talks on Iran’s nuclear programme and says it may reopen the shipping lane – but caveated that it would then start charging tolls for transit.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The calculus behind this barely changed offer may be that “elements of the Iranian regime” think their blockade can impose sufficient economic and political costs to elicit US concessions, the ISW says in its latest war update.

News.title: Met Office forecasts -5C deep freeze as every inch of UK sees temperature plunge
News.content:
Met Office forecasts -5C deep freeze as every inch of UK sees temperature plunge

Met Office weather forecasters say temperatures could plunge to -5C in some parts of the UK this week as an unseasonably cold spell follows on from sizzling 26C heat

View 2 Images Anomaly maps show temperatures will drop well below the seasonal average on Tuesday (Image: WXCHARTS)

Despite temperatures soaring to 26C this week, the Met Office says the mercury could soon plummet well below 0C.

‌



The national weather agency’s forecast today said temperatures overnight on Tuesday could plummet as low as -5C in northern areas and -1C in southern areas. On Wednesday overnight lows of -3C are possible across the country.

‌



The Met Office expects daytime temperatures to peak at 18C on Tuesday before tumbling to 15C on Wednesday - a far cry from the sizzling sun we have experienced in recent days.

‌



Temperature anomaly maps for Tuesday show huge areas of blue across Scotland, Northern Ireland, North Wales, northern England and eastern areas. This indicates where temperatures will be far lower than is expected for this time of year.

View 2 Images The GFS weather model shows temperatures struggling to rise above 8C anywhere on Wednesday morning (Image: WXCHARTS)

UK weather maps show shock snow will hit 26 counties across two days – full list READ MORE :

The GFS weather model shows the highest temperature in the entire country could be just 8C on Wednesday morning. This represents a significant drop off from this week across every part of the UK.

‌



The Met Office forecast for Tuesday to Thursday says conditions will be “turning cooler for all as northerly winds set in across the UK”. We can expect “some showers at times”, although “these [will be] lighter and fewer than the weekend”.

The BBC forecast states: “On Tuesday, much of the UK will be dry with variable cloud, but there will be showers in the south-west and parts of the north.

“Wednesday is expected to be generally cloudy with a few scattered showers in the far north and across the west. Thursday looks to bring further showers to northern and western areas, while the east remain mostly dry with some sunny spells. Windier.”

Article continues below

Thankfully, the Met Office expects temperatures to return to around average later this month. Its forecast for May 7 to May 16 says "a changeable theme" is likely with most places set for "some rain or showers at times, but also some drier, brighter weather".

The forecast adds: "The emphasis on wetter conditions may be more towards the south and east at first, with low pressure perhaps more likely towards the south or east of the UK, before shifting further north later in the period as low pressure becomes more likely to set up to the north or northeast of the UK.

"After a cold start to the period, especially in the north, temperatures are likely to return to around average later."

News.title: Queen Camilla shocks royal fans with ‘incredibly normal’ return from state visit
News.content:
Queen Camilla shocks royal fans with ‘incredibly normal’ return from state visit

After spending a whirlwind four days in the United States, Camilla has returned to UK shores with shocked fans spotting her walking casually through the airport

View 3 Images After four days in the US, Camilla has returned to the UK (Image: WireImage)

After spending four busy days in the United States, King Charles and Queen Camilla ’s state visit has come to an end. Last week, Their Majesties attended engagements in Washington DC alongside President Trump, before travelling to New York and Virginia for more events.

‌



As the whirlwind trip came to a close on Thursday evening, Charles flew to Bermuda for further royal engagements, while Camilla travelled back to the UK. And as the Queen made her way back to Britain, many onlookers were shocked to see her strolling casually through an airport terminal, with her security on either side of her.

‌



View 3 Images Queen Camilla was spotted in an airport leaving the United States (Image: WireImage)

‌



Camilla was sighted in the lounge of Washington Dulles International Airport on Thursday, still wearing the blue ensemble she wore to officially farewell the President and First Lady of the United States earlier that day, as she made her way back to the UK.

One onlooker filmed the moment the Queen walked by and posted it to Instagram with the caption: “Just the Queen casually walking past me at the airport.” The post was quickly flooded with comments, as one person praised the lack of "fuss and drama" in the exit, while others admired her "unruffled and relaxed" demeanour.

Camilla’s US exit was a lot more subdued that the King’s, as he arrived at the Joint Base Andrew’s military base in Maryland on board Donald Trump ’s helicopter, arriving to an honour guard.

‌



Charles was met by Chief of Protocol at the US Ambassador Monica Crowley and UK Ambassador Christian Turner, who officially farewelled the monarch before he boarded the plane to Bermuda.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

The King was given an armed forces full honour cordon, red carpet, and music US Airforce Band he waved from the top of the plane steps, before disappearing inside to end his US visit.

‌



Queen Camilla also received praise elsewhere during the state visit, as President Trump paid her a compliment out the front of the White House during Their Majesties’ departure.

The King and Queen formally farewelled Donald and Melania Trump on Wednesday in Washington DC. As the Trumps greeted Charles and Camilla as they arrived by car on the South Portico, the US leader and the monarch exchanged pleasantries and compliments before they headed inside the White House to formally bring a close to their visit.

View 3 Images Queen Camilla and President Trump at the White House (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



And as lip reader Jeremy Freeman told the Mirror, President Trump was full of praise for Queen Camilla. As the two couples stood outside the White House, Trump said to the King: “It’s been good. It’s been important. Look at everybody,” before pointing to Camilla and saying: “I don’t know how she does it, she’s amazing”.

The President then turned to the Queen and said: “It was fantastic. I look forward to seeing you again. Thank you for making it a success. Love to the grandchildren”.

News.title: Primary school teacher who 'filmed children on hidden toilet camera' is pictured
News.content:
Primary school teacher who 'filmed children on hidden toilet camera' is pictured

Primary school teacher Timothy Blamires, 33, is accused of putting a camera in the toilets of Kingswood Primary School in south Melbourne to film pupils, a court heard

View 2 Images Timothy Blamires has been denied bail (Image: 7 News)

A primary school teacher is alleged to have used a camera to film pupils in the boys' toilets.

‌



Timothy Blamires, 33, appeared via videolink at Moorabbin Magistrates’ Court in south Melbourne, and was reportedly refused bail over fears he could tamper with evidence.

‌



He was arrested last Tuesday and has been charged with producing and possessing child abuse material after a camera was found at Kingswood Primary School, Dingley Village.

‌



Prosecutors allege a cleaner found a hidden camera inside an odour dispenser in the toilets, which was pointed at the urinals. The cleaner put it in a bag and left it on the headteacher’s desk.

View 2 Images Kingswood Primary School (file) (Image: ABC News)

UK airlines set to make major flight schedule changes this summer READ MORE :

Blamires is said to have taken the camera and put it inside a drawer in a sick bay at the school. Following his arrest, the odour dispenser was allegedly found inside his bag at the school.

‌



Police are understood to have taken electronic devices including laptops, phones and tablets from Blamires’ home as part of the investigation.

And it is alleged that footage on the camera showed Blamires setting up the device as well as children using the toilet.

Magistrate Timothy Gattuso said he would not release Blamires on bail because there was an "unacceptable risk" he could interfere with witnesses and destroy evidence.

‌



The magistrate also claimed Blamires had given passwords to police that “were not accurate”.

Blamires' brother is understood to have offered a AU$50,000 surety for the defendant to be given bail and said he would live with him to ensure he did not violate any of his conditions, but the prosecution argued that he was a risk to the public and may try to destroy evidence.

Denying bail, Mr Gattuso pointed to the allegation that Blamires tried to hide the camera after it was found by a cleaner. "You appear to have removed the device that had been located in the toilets by the cleaner, from the principal's office, and apparently hid it," he told the court.

Article continues below

A mother of one of the pupils at the school attended the court hearing and said how "difficult" it had been, reported ABC News.

"I think I was the first one to break down in the court room. It was extremely difficult but I needed to see it," she said. "I just needed to be here... just to be able to process this whole situation."

News.title: 'Suspicious' Bristol explosion declared major incident as 2 dead – FULL police update
News.content:
'Suspicious' Bristol explosion declared major incident as 2 dead – FULL police update

Two adults have died after an explosion at a house in the Frenchay area of Bristol this morning - police are treating it as 'suspicious' and a major incident has been declared

Bristol: Police at scene of deadly explosion in Frenchay

Two people have died in a 'suspicious' house explosion in Bristol. Police have declared a major incident and deployed bomb disposal units.

‌



The explosion was reported at a property in Sterncourt Road in the Frenchay area at around 6.30am. Armed police were spotted and residents have been moved to an emergency “temporary rest centre” in the nearby Snuff Mill Harvester pub.

‌



Locals heard a loud "bang" this morning before smoke was seen surging from one of the houses. Avon and Somerset Police set up a white tent at the site and the cordon was later extended to cover the corner of Froomshaw Road.

‌



View 2 Images Police at the scene in Bristol following the explosion (Image: PAUL GILLIS / Reach Plc)

Bristol explosion updates: Two dead as suspicious blast declared major incident READ MORE :

Jet2 announces major 'first' for airline in huge boost to British holidaymakers READ MORE :

The force said the incident is being treated as suspicious, and that a major incident has been declared. The explosion is not being treated as terror related, and police are not looking for anyone else. Police are however carrying out inquiries at a property in Speedwell, believed to be linked to the explosion.

One resident who has been moved to the Harvester pub said he heard a loud "bang" at 6.30am and went outside, before being told to "get inside" by armed police. He said neighbours spotted smoke billowing from one of the houses.

‌



View 2 Images A bomb squad has been deployed (Image: PAUL GILLIS / Reach Plc)

Avon and Somerset Police statement in full after Bristol house explosion

A cordon remains in place while emergency services respond to an incident in Bristol.

An explosion was reported at a residential address in Sterncourt Road at about 6.30am today (Sunday 3 May).

‌



The cause of the incident is being treated as suspicious, and a major incident has been declared.

Two adults have died at the address and their families have been updated. Emergency services are following well-rehearsed plans in response to this incident.

Our enquiries are at an early stage, but at this point we are not looking for anyone else in connection with this incident.

‌



The cordon has been put in place as a precaution to help keep the public safe. People living within that cordon are therefore being evacuated to a temporary rest centre. There is not believed to be any significant damage to other properties.

Officers are also carrying out enquiries at a property in Speedwell linked to this incident.

Given the recent change to the UK threat level, we would like to reassure the public from the outset we are not treating this as a suspected terrorist incident.

Article continues below

We ask people not to speculate around the circumstances and continue to encourage the public to avoid the area while emergency services respond to this incident.

News.title: Harry and Meghan's horror during King's Trump visit yet 'united' with Charles
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Harry and Meghan's horror during King's Trump visit yet 'united' with Charles

While the monarch did not see his son or grandchildren during his US visit, one royal expert believes the Duke of Sussex would be ‘quietly proud’ of one major aspect of the King’s stateside trip

View 4 Images Prince Harry with King Charles (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

King Charles has wrapped his whirlwind trip the United States, in which he and Queen Camilla attended back-to-back engagements in Washington DC, Virginia and New York over four days. While it was the King’s first time in America for many years, he did not journey to the West Coast to see his estranged son Prince Harry, or his grandchildren Archie and Lilibet.

‌



Harry’s relationship with his father remains strained, as the pair have only seen each other a handful of times in recent years. The last time the father and son met face-to-face was in September last year, when the Duke of Sussex was in London for the annual WellChild awards.

‌



William and Kate share unseen photo of Princess Charlotte to mark her 11th birthday READ MORE :

King Charles’ iconic bearded bodyguard makes huge decision about his royal future READ MORE :

View 4 Images Prince Harry and King Charles' relationship has been strained for several years (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



It had been established months before Charles embarked on his US trip that he would not have a chance to see his son, daughter-in-law Meghan Markle or their children during his state visit.

However, former BBC royal commentator Jennie Bond believes Harry would have had conflicting feelings over seeing the King’s highly publicised trip in the country he has called home for over six years.

Jennie told the Mirror : “I don’t think it would have been any surprise to Harry that there was no opportunity to see his father during the state visit. But it must have been a rather surreal experience to watch his dad being feted in the country which is now Harry‘s home, and yet not to see him.

‌



View 4 Images Last week, Charles spent four days in the US on a state visit (Image: AP)

“Of course, in reality, they were still thousands of miles apart and the two of them have not even met when they’ve been within a mile of one another in London. So it was never going to happen.”

The royal expert believes that there is still the possibility of the father and son mending their relationship, but it would likely be behind closed doors as they build bridges after years of estrangement. “Their relationship is still strained and, if and when a further meeting happens, I’m sure it won’t be in such a public arena as this exceptionally high profile visit,” Jennie explained.

‌



While Harry has not been a working royal since 2020, he and his father have many shared interests and passions as they both carry out similar charity work. However, Jennie believes that Harry watching his father carry out such philanthropic work in his home country may have felt surreal.

View 4 Images Charles did not visit his son or grandchildren during his rare stateside trip (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

She said: “Harry is on record as saying he believes his father and brother are trapped in their royal existence. And, only last week, he said how important it was to have the right to hold truth to power and to say what he believes. So he may have felt rather conflicted watching the King in action.

‌



“On the one hand, he probably felt that the President didn’t deserve all the reflected glory of having the King and Queen at the White House. But I think he would’ve been quietly proud of the way Charles skilfully delivered some quite pointed and political ripostes to the things Trump has been saying.

“Harry stands united with his father on the need to support Ukraine, for example. And he would have appreciated his father‘s nuanced putdown of Trump‘s insults about British service men and women and our naval power.”

‌



During the visit, President Trump did not miss the opportunity to sling an insult at Meghan Markle - with whom he has been engaged in a war of words online for several years, as well as Harry - and Jennie believes this dig would’ve only further solidified Harry’s desire to not be a part of the Royal Family.

Jennie said: “Of course, outside the immediate environs of the visit, it has offered Trump the opportunity to sling a few more insults in the Sussex‘s direction – particularly at Meghan. And that will have further antagonised the couple.

“So, whilst the visit has undoubtedly gone some way to improving relations between the United States and the UK, it has done nothing to help the relationship between the President and Harry and Meghan.”

News.title: I saw health red flags when on toilet - then doctor's phone call left me numb
News.content:
I saw health red flags when on toilet - then doctor's phone call left me numb

Bronwyn, 27, first noticed something was wrong on the loo but was told her symptoms were probably just piles

View 4 Images Bronwyn one week after her diagnosis (Image: Jam Press)

A mum was left feeling 'numb' after a phone call from her doctor following health symptoms she experienced on the toilet. Bronwyn Tagg first noticed something was wrong shortly after giving birth to her son, Austin, now two.

‌



The 27 year old started experiencing bleeding when using the toilet, which she says she flagged to her GP. "They didn't examine me but said it was most probably piles after having a vaginal birth," Bronwyn, from Cambridge, said.

‌



"After that, I started to have quite frequent diarrhoea so I had a gluten tolerance test, which came back negative. In the beginning of 2024, I started to get pretty horrendous tummy aches leaving me barrelled over, unable to move kind of tummy aches.

‌



View 4 Images Bronwyn now (Image: Jam Press)

"So I went back to the GP. I'd previously had ovarian cysts so assumed that's what it was.

"The GP arranged an ultrasound which did show a cyst on my left ovary so I had a test for ovarian cancers but the results were normal. I was referred to gynaecology for the pain.

‌



"In February 2025, I saw a gynaecologist and explained my symptoms who said it could be endometriosis so arranged an MRI." The MRI revealed a 40mm lesion in her rectum.

Bronwyn was urgently referred on a two-week cancer pathway and had a colonoscopy in May 2025, during which doctors removed the entire polyp. The mum said: "Two weeks later, I had a phone call whilst doing my shopping.

"They asked me to come in the following day for my results and to bring someone for support. I instantly knew it was bad news.

‌



"I felt so numb doing the rest of the shopping, my 18 month old sat in the trolley just thinking 'what am I going to do?' We were called into the room and it was really quiet and sombre and that's when the consultant said 'I'm really sorry to have to tell you that the polyp we removed was cancer'.

"The rest of the appointment is a complete blur - I didn't take anything in. I had no questions at that time, my husband was next to me in tears but I just felt nothing."

I was told it had already knocked years off my life

Bronwyn, who is also mum to Josie, five, chose to undergo surgery to remove part of her rectum and have a stoma fitted after the bowel cancer diagnosis. The dental nurse said: "A consultant put it very bluntly and said that this will have already knocked a few years off my life."

‌



Six weeks later, further devastating news awaited Bronwyn and her husband Glen, 27. Three of the 12 lymph nodes removed during surgery tested positive, meaning her cancer was reclassified as stage three.

She faced chemotherapy as a result. Bronwyn endured exhaustion, nausea, nerve pain and emotional turmoil, all while continuing to care for her young children. Bronwyn said: "Chemotherapy was a lot more challenging mentally than it was physically.

View 4 Images Bronwyn today (Image: Jam Press)

‌



"Don't get me wrong, it had been incredibly tough physically too. I struggled with exhaustion, nausea, and peripheral neuropathy and pain.

"And I found it so hard hyping myself up to go in for treatment that was going to make me feel rubbish. Chemo made being a mum quite hard.

"Josie started school in September and I started chemotherapy the week after. Whilst my husband is amazing at supporting where he can, he has had to continue working hard earning money so I still had to do the majority of childcare.

‌



"Friends and family have helped with schools runs, dinners and play dates." One of the most difficult aspects, she explains, was discussing her illness with her five-year-old daughter Josie.

She said: "We tried not to convey that we were scared. We started off my telling her I needed an operation to remove something that wasn't very nice from mummy's belly.

"When I woke up with a stoma, I really wasn't sure how she was going to take it. Thankfully the stoma nurses at the hospital are beyond amazing and supportive.

‌



"They provided me with a teddy and a story book which helped explain mummy's new body. She was very unsure at first, asked all sorts of curious questions as any five year old would like 'does it hurt? why do you have a bag? why does it look like that?'

"And I was just really honest with her. I change and empty my bag in front of her and will shower with her in the room.

"I think it's good for her to realise not all body's look the same and that's ok. Even now, nine months post surgery, she still asks questions about how it works.

‌



"When I started chemotherapy, I explained to her that I was going to have some very important medicine at the hospital. I said I would have to go every two weeks for one day and that the medicine would make me tired and feel a bit sick.

"But I explained it was important for me to have it so that the bad stuff in mummy's tummy hopefully doesn't come back. She's been amazing throughout all of this.

"So helpful and brave. I only recently told her that I had cancer.

‌



"I think I really wanted to protect her to begin with but really it's about being open and honest with your children. She asked me if I was going to die and Glen found that quite tricky."

View 4 Images Watch out for the symptoms and contact a health professional if you have concerns (Image: Getty)

Bronwyn has since finished chemotherapy and is now awaiting the results of a recent scan to establish whether she is in remission. She said: "I'm really hopeful that we're done but I know that we won't ever go back to how life was before.

‌



"It's a new normal. A normal where we now understand just how fragile life is.

"I don't sweat the small stuff any more." Following the death of Married At First Sight star Mel Schilling last month, Bronwyn is speaking out to help raise awareness. She said: "With the recent passing of Mel Schilling, I know that being in remission doesn't always mean it's done and finished.

"I think this whole crazy year has taught me to value my own time, to be a bit more selfish, say no to things I don't want to waste my energy with and to say yes to everything that excites me. I plan on making some incredible memories with my children over the next new years."

‌



Bronwyn is encouraging others to keep pushing if something doesn't feel right. She added: "For anyone noticing any symptoms, I would say go and get them checked with the GP.

"If they are disregarded because of their age, they need to persist. Early diagnosis saves lives."

Symptoms of bowel cancer - NHS

The NHS website says the main symptoms of bowel cancer may include:

‌



needing to poo more or less often than usual for you

often feeling like you need to poo, even if you've just been to the toilet

bleeding from your bottom

tummy pain

losing weight without trying

blood in your poo, which may look red or black

changes in your poo, such as having softer poo, diarrhoea or constipation that is not usual for you

feeling very tired or short of breath – these are signs of anaemia, which can be caused by bowel cancer

a lump in your tummy

bloating

The NHS advises people that if you have any symptoms of bowel cancer for 3 weeks or more, you should see a GP. They say: "Try not to be embarrassed. The doctor or nurse will be used to talking about these symptoms."

You should ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if your poo is black or dark red or you have bloody diarrhoea

Article continues below

You can call 111 or get help from 111 online. But go to A&E or call 999 if you're bleeding non-stop from your bottom, or if there is a lot of blood, for example, the toilet water turns red or you see large blood clots.

News.title: Trump must learn lessons and not invade Iran, warns US Navy Seal who claims to have shot Bin Laden
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Trump must learn lessons and not invade Iran, warns US Navy Seal who claims to have shot Bin Laden

Today former US Navy Seal Matt Bissonette, who only unmasked his true identity last year after years of protecting his identity with a pseudonym, reveals the details of an extraordinary mission which toppled Bin Laden on May 2, 2011

View 5 Images Matt Bissonnette has spoken out on the 15th anniversary of Bin Laden's death (Image: 60 Minutes)

The US Navy Seal who shot Osama Bin Laden has demanded his country “learn their lessons” from conflicts in Afghanistan and Iraq to prevent escalating a bloody war with Iran.

‌



Former special forces serviceman Matt Bissonette - one of a crack team to execute the Al Qaeda leader in a covert operation in 2011 - has urged President Donald Trump not to send “boots on the ground” into the Middle East and avoid needless deaths.

‌



In an interview to mark 15 years since the toppling of Bin Laden, Matt has told how he has still not processed what happened on the infamous Operation Neptune Spear, reveals how the assignment left him with severe injuries and tells of he discovered the evil Taliban leader’s secret disguise… a bottle of Just For Men hair dye.

‌



As tensions in the Middle East remain on a knife edge, Matt – now 50 - who did 13 combat tours in Iraq and Afghanistan between 2001 and 2012, told the Mirror: “It is essential we learn our lessons. I'm glad they're not invading Iran like we did Iraq. We're not building bases and putting tanks on the ground and sending thousands of soldiers in like we did in Iraq and Afghanistan. We're not doing it and I'm at least glad to see that.

View 5 Images Matt says he shot Bin Laden during Operation Neptune Spear (Image: mattbissonnette.com)

Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei issues horror new threat to Americans READ MORE :

Inside daring raid that killed Osama Bin Laden - from helicopter crash and finding his hair dye to fatal shot READ MORE :

“I’m hoping it shows that just maybe we've learned a few things. Because I can tell you from first-hand experience, the way we did it in Iraq and Afghanistan did not work. Too many of my friends died and too many lives were lost.”

‌



On bringing down Bin Laden, he said: “I try not to be defined by that moment but I joined the Navy Seals just before he orchestrated 9/11. It was a driving goal to bring him down. So it is still hard to process I fired shots that brought Bin Laden down. It was a remarkable mission and it’s hard to believe it is 15 years on. I’m proud we relieved the world of one of its worst tyrants.”

Today Matt, who only unmasked his true identity last year after years of protecting his identity with a pseudonym, revealed the details of an extraordinary mission which toppled Bin Laden on May 2, 2011 – as the 23-strong special forces team scrambled from the US to Afghanistan and then to Bin Laden’s lair in Pakistan.

Extraordinarily, he revealed how he broke his neck as his team’s helicopter crashed as they attempted to land near their target yet still carried out the 40-minute raid on Bin Laden’s secret bunker – killing the despot and his son Khalid.

‌



View 5 Images A US soldier from the 2nd Squadron, 2nd Stryker Cavalry Regiment, kicks the door of an adandoned house in Baghdad, 11 January 2008 (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

Our interview comes days after US president Donald Trump hinted he would escalate his country’s action in the Middle East after he took to his Truth Social page to declare ‘No more Mr Nice Guy’ towards Iran along with an AI-image of himself holding an assault rifle against a backdrop of missiles striking buildings.

Matt, who grew up in Alaska, joined the Navy Seals in 1999. While on his first tour, terrorists directed by Osama Bin Laden crashed passenger planes into New York and the Pentagon – killing almost 3,000 at 9/11.

‌



Matt said: “From that day, it was very clear that it was Osama Bin Laden that we were after. We had a focus – ‘get this guy.’ We would regularly talk about getting him and making sure we brought him down.”

As he rose the ranks of the Navy Seals, he toured Iraq and Afghanistan 13 times – conducted many covert missions – and averaged 250 days away on service a year for a decade. In total he estimates he spent around “three or four years put together in the countries”.

In all these years Bin Laden evaded international special forces who tried to bring him to justice. But in April 2011, he and the rest of the team he was in were pulled into a high-security meeting when they were told about intel about a possible hiding place in Pakistan.

‌



View 5 Images Osama bin Laden (L) sits with his adviser Ayman al-Zawahiri in an undated photo (Image: Getty Images)

After a week of training, the team were scrambled to Afghanistan before boarding a helicopter bound for a compound – believed to contain wanted Al Queda targets. The 23-man team also had a translator and an explosives dog with them.

He said: “We were poised in Afghanistan waiting for orders from President Obama to give us the thumbs up. It was the most experienced of teams – everyone had been on hundreds if not thousands of covert missions. We were meant to launch the mission the day prior but it was delayed.”

‌



But the next day the weather was significantly warmer and as they made their descent towards their target, the high temperatures played havoc with the landing – sending the chopper spiralling to the ground.

Matt said: “I was sitting in the doorway when we crashed. We were supposed to hover, push a rope out, slide down the rope and go to work, but that never happened. We got very lucky. We hit the ground and then it was time to jump out and go to work. We were now in the compound in one of the houses outside the main house – it was a house of one of Bin Laden’s facilitators. The first door we got to, I ended up being shot at through.”

Soon the door opened and a woman and her child were sent to open it. The Seals forced their way in found a stairway, moving the women and children to safety, and found a reinforced metal door in front of a staircase.

‌



Matt said: “That gave another sign they were trying to hide something. We blew through the door, there was no power, no lights, it was very quiet – not like you see in the movies at all.”

Intel had informed them that they would first find Bin Laden’s son Khalid on the first floor of the main house. Very quickly, they saw a man moving.

Matt added: “The point man – our man at the front - whispered out, ‘Khalid’, at which point he poked his head around the door and was shot. It was Khalid and he had an AK47 in his hands. It was amazing bit of calmness from our point man.

‌



“We then headed up to the third floor and I remember another head popping out. Our point man took a couple of shots and that head disappeared into the room. I then shot him again on the floor. It was Bin Laden. But at that point we were just looking for threats we didn’t have time to identify him. There were two women in there who we now know were his two wives. We questioned the women and eventually they revealed it was Bin Laden. We had to check his face. He was tall and had a very dark beard. I recognised his nose but the dark hair threw me.

“There was no grey in the beard. But when I searched his bathroom, I found just for men hair dye. He had been dying his beard. We had Bin Laden.”

“What struck me about the house was that Bin Laden’s room was incredibly tidy while the rest of the house was a mess. I went through his closet and the clothes hanging in there were perfectly evenly spaced like a military boot camp.”

‌



They collected up Bin Laden’s body, collected any evidence they could find including computers, moved the women and kids to a safe place and blew up their own crashed helicopter before scrambling away in another chopper. They debriefed in Afghanistan before being flown home to the US.

Matt said: “Our boss just said, ‘well done guys, have two days off’. We just went home. It felt so weird being at home knowing what we had done. I couldn’t sleep. Everyone knew what we’d done. I went to put the bins out on one of the days and a neighbour came up and gave me a hug and said, ‘I guess you never know who your neighbours are.’”

As Matt tried to come to terms with the mission and the adrenaline wore off, the severity of his injuries started to reveal themselves.

‌



He said: “I had a torn rotator cuff and needed surgery and then that's when I really started figuring out my neck had more issues. I've had a fusion, two artificial discs, five neck surgeries. It was all from the helicopter crash.”

A few months after the mission, Matt was dealt a hammer blow when a third of the command group he worked in were killed in the Extortion helicopter crash, which killed 22 in Afghanistan.

He said: “It showed how life had gone from huge highs to huge lows. I lost so many friends. It confirmed my decision to leave the Navy Seals. We had Bin Laden and getting him was the reason I stayed with command so long.”

‌



View 5 Images A copy of "No Easy Day", an account of the killing of Osama Bin Laden on May 2, 2011 (Image: Getty Images)

In 2012, Matt, who has now started a new life rearing wagyu cow, wrote a book under his pseudonym Mark Owen about the operation but faced the wrath of US officials for revealing information which was deemed classified.

He has now written another book called No Easy Way with his real name attached – talking about the trauma he has been through.

Article continues below

He said: “My journey as a Nay Seal had the most remarkable arc. It went from 9/11 to my last mission being killing the man who orchestrated 9/11. I feel very proud but as a world we must learn our lessons from previous conflicts.”

Matt’s book No Easy Way is out later this month

News.title: Gorka Marquez's plan B after Strictly exit - and clue no-one spotted in statement
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Gorka Marquez's plan B after Strictly exit - and clue no-one spotted in statement

As Gorka Márquez becomes the latest Strictly Come Dancing star to quit the dancefloor, the Mirror takes a look at the pro-dancer's potential Plan B as he waltzes towards a new and 'intriguing' chapter

View 5 Images Gorka Márquez's departure announcement has been described as a 'calculated repositioning'

After ten years, Gorka Márquez is bidding farewell to Strictly Come Dancing, with a somewhat cryptic post that has kept people guessing. And one line contains a particularly 'heavy clue' as to what will come next.

‌



This comes at a time of huge upheaval in the ballroom. Gorka is the fifth professional dancer to bow out ahead of the upcoming series, while the shock departure of presenting duo Claudia Winkleman and Tess Daly marks something of a reset.

‌



In a bombshell statement, the 35-year-old Spanish star explained that this move follows his decision last year "to step down as a full-time professional" over "scheduling conflicts between Strictly and Dancing with the Stars Spain".

‌



Sharing a poignant black and white snap of him walking towards a studio door, back turned and expression unseen, Gorka revealed, "I've decided that now is the time to hang up my dance shoes and say goodbye to Strictly Come Dancing." For many loyal Strictly viewers, this is the real end of a golden era.

The charismatic Spanish dancer, who met and fell in love with his now partner, 2017 contestant Gemma Atkinson, during Strictly rehearsals, has long been a fan favourite. His departure, which follows a bumpy period of scandals in the Strictly studio, will likely come as a blow to those hoping for some familiarity in the 2026 season.

Gorka Marquez's statement in full as Strictly Come Dancing star quits after 10 years READ MORE :

View 5 Images The Strictly star dropped the bombshell in an Instagram post, to the dismay of fans (Image: Instagram)

‌



As for Gorka, the first part of his farewell message strikes a breezy, positive note, throwing a "very polite veil" over any rumoured issues behind the scenes. Expressing gratitude for his time on the hit Saturday night show, Gorka wrote: "I will always be incredibly grateful to Strictly and the BBC for everything. Being part of the show has been so much more than just a professional opportunity—over the past 10 years, it allowed me to build a career from my passion, find love, start a family, and make lifelong friends. For that, I will forever be thankful."

Analysing the tone of this opening, leading body language and communications expert Judi James told the Mirror: "This statement is part professional ‘conscious uncoupling’-style cliché as he refers to ‘always being incredibly grateful to Strictly’; the ‘sharing the love’, and of course the reference to the ‘incredible family’ of Strictly, all of which throws a very polite veil over any suspicions or potential rumours of any behind-the-scenes problems, letting the fans know he’s leaving on the best terms with only good things to say about the experience"

But it's the second part of the statement that Judi finds to be most "intriguing". In his announcement, Gorka alluded to what will come next, sharing: "Although I’m stepping away from the dance floor, I can’t wait to dance on the Strictly Pro Tour starting this week and continue being part of this incredible family. Now it’s time to take a step back, enjoy the sidelines… and hopefully hold up a few paddles and give out some tens along the way."

‌



View 5 Images During his ten-year run on the show, Gorka met and fell in love with his now partner Gemma Atkinson (Image: Dave Nelson / Daily Mirror)

He concluded: "Thank you to everyone who has supported me and shared their love throughout this incredible journey. Keep dancing." Noting Gorka's wording here, Judi remarked that there appeared to be somewhat of a "conflict" within his messaging. Judi reflected: "The intriguing aspect of this message, though, comes from the non-specific, hazy hints about what his job might be in future.

"He says he’s stepping down as a full-time professional, which should mean he’s stopping dancing, but then there’s still the references to ‘the Stars Spain’ and dancing on the Strictly Pro Tour, which sounds in conflict with his claims to be ‘hanging up’ his dance shoes."

‌



She continued: "Fans of the very popular dancer might also be confused by what sounds like a cryptic reference to maybe returning in the role of a judge. Is he teasing the fans when he refers to ‘hopefully holding up a few paddles and giving a few tens along the way’? He could just mean he’ll be watching and scoring from the sofa in front of his own TV, but this does read like a heavy clue to a new career as a judge, especially with the ‘Keep dancing’ sign off."

View 5 Images PR to the stars, Mayah Riaz advised that Gorka's decision 'feels far less 'sudden' than it’s being framed' (Image: BBC)

Gorka was absent from the last series due to his commitments on the Spanish version of Strictly, where he sits on the judging panel. The dancer subsequently faced rumours about his future on the British show, with The Sun previously reporting how he was set to be axed back in March, with producers allegedly wanting a “fresh start” for the BBC1 show.

‌



Meanwhile, speaking recently with The Sun, a source claimed Gorka had initially wanted to quit back in 2022 but was persuaded to stay by BBC bosses "digging deep with a new deal". As per this source, dancers regularly got the "seven-year itch" to move elsewhere, a longing that was worsened for Gorka following a "painful moment". In 2022, he and partner Helen Skelton reached the final, only to be bested by Jowita Przystal and Hamza Yassin.

According to this source, "It was a really painful moment when he didn’t win with Helen. He threw everything he could at winning that year, and it still wasn’t enough. It was heartbreaking for him." They noted that, since then, as Gorka had "secretly struggled" to find "the perfect celebrity partner to match his high standards", his exit won't have come as a surprise to those in the know.

So could there be more to the narrative than meets the eye? The Mirror also heard from PR to the stars, Mayah Riaz, who advised that, in her professional opinion, Gorka's decision "feels far less 'sudden' than it’s being framed." According to Mayah: "When a long-standing professional like Gorka exits Strictly after a decade, it is almost always the result of a slow shift behind the scenes rather than one impulsive decision. I feel the cryptic tone of his statement is actually quite telling. It suggests a careful balancing act between gratitude and quiet frustration."

‌



Fellow professionals Karen Hauer, Nadiya Bychkova, Luba Mushtuk, and Michelle Tsiakkas have all quit the dancefloor ahead of the 2026 season, in a huge shake-up of the long-running BBC show. Adding to this sense of unease is the feeling by some that Gorka has been 'sidelined'. Mayah told us: "There is a narrative gaining traction that he may have been sidelined without a consistent partner, and in TV terms, visibility is everything. If talent feels they are no longer front and centre, it can start to chip away at both morale and brand value. In that context, leaving on his own terms can be a power move for him rather than a setback.

View 5 Images It's thought this move could be all about regaining 'control' (Image: PA)

"From a PR lens, this is about control. It is much better to step away while your audience is still asking questions than to fade out unnoticed. There is a real sense here of 'leave them wanting more', which is a classic celebrity play. It keeps him relevant, it sparks speculation, and crucially, it protects his long-term positioning."

‌



As explained by Mayah, "timing" is another "key factor" here, especially when taking into account the ever-shifting pace of the outwardly glittering industry. She observed: "If he already had another opportunity lined up, this becomes less of a risk and more of a strategic pivot. In today’s entertainment landscape, talent needs to think like brands. Loyalty to one show for ten years is rare, but so is staying past the point where you feel undervalued.

In terms of impact, I’d say that this puts a subtle spotlight back on Strictly itself. When a popular professional exits with even a hint of ambiguity, audiences start to question what is happening behind the scenes. That kind of narrative can quietly snowball if not handled carefully. All in all, I’d say this is definitely less a shock exit and more a calculated repositioning. He has chosen to close the chapter while he still holds the pen.”

Strictly Come Dancing has issued the following statement on Gorka's departure: "We would like to extend our sincere thanks to Gorka for his exceptional contribution to Strictly Come Dancing over the years. Since joining the show in 2016, Gorka has been a hugely popular member of the professional dancer line-up, known for his passion, charisma and exceptional choreography.

Article continues below

"As well as being part of our Strictly family, it’s been heartwarming to see him start his own family during his time with us, and that journey reflects the same warmth, commitment and character he has always brought to the show. We are incredibly grateful for his dedication to the series over the years and are so proud to see him shining in his judging role on Bailando con las Estrellas in Spain. We wish him continued success and happiness in everything that’s to come."
